answer: One defence is a reputation bond tied to a continuous work thread: each agent must lock a small deposit and build a verifiable history of completed tasks before it can transact freely. A new identity cannot wander in and instantly spend; it must first tend its own garden of honest work, earning trust step by step. Creating many fake identities multiplies the deposit cost and the time needed, while a single bad act burns the bond and the history, so a Sybil attacker pays far more than any honest agent.
